affected_hardware: CUDA systems using FP8/INT8 dynamic quantization
affected_kernel: dynamic_per_token FP8 and dynamic INT8 quant custom ops
evidence_snippet: RuntimeError: Expected input.is_contiguous() to be true, but got false.
rationale: The dynamic FP8/INT8 quant kernels require contiguous input, but model evaluation could pass non-contiguous tensors. The fix enforces contiguity before invoking the custom ops.
counterfactual_rationale: Unit tests that pass non-contiguous or strided tensors into the dynamic quantization ops would have revealed the precondition violation.

introducing_evidence: The NPU MoE refactor (#25663) moved `top_k` from being derived at runtime
evidence_snippet: TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'int' and 'NoneType'
rationale: The NPU MoE refactor cached top_k from config, but OLMoE did not provide it, so None reached the routing kernel initialization. The fix re-derives top_k from runtime top-k tensors.
counterfactual_rationale: An NPU serving smoke for OLMoE after the MoE refactor would have caught the startup TypeError.

affected_kernel: FlashInfer CUTLASS fused MoE autotuning bound
introducing_evidence: Previously, #34542 refactored ... and passed the CUDA graph max capture size
evidence_snippet: using it can select a tuning configuration for the wrong token range and thus cause suboptimal perf unexpectedly
rationale: A prior refactor passed CUDA graph capture size as the MoE autotune token bound, selecting poor tuning configurations. The fix partially reverts that argument to the FlashInfer default.
counterfactual_rationale: Model-level MoE throughput benchmarks across realistic token bounds and parallel configurations would have detected the performance regression.

affected_kernel: cutlass_fp4_group_mm registration / NVFP4 group MM kernel
evidence_snippet: unconditionally registered in `torch_bindings.cpp` even though its implementation is only compiled when `ENABLE_NVFP4_SM100` is defined, causing undefined symbol errors on Hopper.
rationale: The custom op was registered on Hopper even though its implementation was compiled only for SM100, causing undefined symbols. The fix conditionally registers the op with the kernel implementation.
counterfactual_rationale: A Hopper build/import CI lane for the custom ops would have caught the undefined symbol from unconditional registration.

rationale: FlashInfer NVLink managers sized MNNVL workspace to the DP group while kernels expected the EP group, causing assertion/mismatched allocation when DP size differed from EP size.
counterfactual_rationale: A serving/all-to-all test with TP>1, DP>1, and EP over NVLink would have exposed the group-size workspace mismatch.

affected_kernel: NPU Gemma RMSNorm/logits and chunked batch scheduling paths
evidence_snippet: Fix inference of Gemma 2 and Gemma 3 multimodal scenario with batch > 1 on Ascend devices and Phi3 model problem
rationale: The PR describes NPU-only inference and accuracy fixes for Gemma/Phi models, including batch>1 page alignment and GemmaRMSNorm changes. Details are limited but the failure is hardware/backend specific.
counterfactual_rationale: An NPU model matrix covering Gemma2, Gemma3 multimodal batch>1, and Phi-3 TP sizes would have exposed the accuracy and inference failures.

affected_kernel: EPLB redundant experts with shared expert fusion and Waterfill
evidence_snippet: map those shared weights back to the physical shared slot layout used by FusedMoE
rationale: The summary indicates EPLB redundant expert counts and fused shared-checkpoint weights were mapped with the wrong logical/physical expert layout. The observed failure is not detailed, so confidence is medium.
counterfactual_rationale: A DeepSeek EP/EPLB serving or model-correctness test with redundant experts and shared expert fusion would exercise the logical-to-physical mapping.

affected_hardware: CUDA/ROCm attention backends with CUDA graphs
evidence_snippet: initialize `req_to_token` with `torch.zeros` instead of `torch.empty` to avoid out-of-bound access during cuda graph capture
rationale: Uninitialized req_to_token padding during CUDA graph capture could cause OOB access in attention backends. Zero-initializing the buffer removes the invalid padding values.
counterfactual_rationale: Memcheck/initcheck on a CUDA-graph attention capture would flag use of uninitialized padding or the resulting OOB access.

evidence_snippet: Disable hip sampler temporarily to fix the accuracy issue of deepseek on ROCm platrform.
rationale: The ROCm HIP sampler produced repetitive/incorrect DeepSeek outputs and also triggered an AMD-specific resource error in comments. The fix disables that sampler path until it can be debugged.
counterfactual_rationale: A ROCm generation/accuracy matrix for DeepSeek or gpt-oss with the HIP sampler enabled would have shown the repeated-output failure.

affected_kernel: FlashInfer backend hyperparameter inference and TRTLLM attention selection
evidence_snippet: AssertionError: FlashInfer backend currently only supports models in which all layers share the same values
rationale: FlashInfer global hyperparameter checks ran before TRTLLM attention usage was known, so mixed-hyperparameter models failed unless an environment variable bypassed the check. The fix delays and refines the check.
counterfactual_rationale: A serving or backend-selection test for a mixed-hyperparameter model without VLLM_USE_TRTLLM_ATTENTION would have exposed the assertion.

rationale: This PR changes ROCm CI/test configuration to avoid flaky AITER-stack state leakage by selecting an explicit backend; it does not fix the underlying production kernel behavior.

evidence_snippet: hardcodes the fp8 clamp/scale bound to `224.0` for all ROCm devices, but the fp8 range is device-dependent
rationale: The ROCm quant kernel used the MI300 e4m3fnuz max on gfx95x, wasting half the e4m3fn range and silently degrading FP8 accuracy. The fix uses the resolved device-specific fp8_max and adds a gfx950 test.
counterfactual_rationale: A gfx95x quantization CI test with values near 448 would have caught the wrong device-specific scale; ordinary lower-range inputs could miss it.

affected_kernel: MoE permute/unpermute and FlashInfer AOT build paths
rationale: MoE permute/unpermute kernels introduced by a prior change did not build on CUDA <12, and FlashInfer AOT needed disabling. The fix skips/guards those kernels for CUDA 11.8 and updates availability tests.
counterfactual_rationale: A CUDA 11.8 build-and-test CI lane would have caught the incompatible kernel build before merge.

rationale: The title mentions correction-bias undefined behavior for nvfp4 models, but the PR body is TODO-only and the discussion does not establish an observed failure, symptom, or fix rationale.

affected_hardware: AMD MI355X / ROCm with MoRI and DP attention
affected_kernel: Qwen3.5 fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm, GDN, sampler, and MoE EP routing paths
evidence_snippet: HIP rejects it with `invalid configuration argument`
rationale: Idle DP-attention ranks launched zero-sized Triton/AITER grids on HIP, and MoRI was routed through a TP path that could all-reduce mismatched shapes. The fix guards zero-token launches and routes MoRI through EP combine.
counterfactual_rationale: A ROCm hardware matrix with DP-attention cases that include empty ranks would catch the HIP-only zero-grid failure; zero-size randomized tests would add focused coverage.
